title: What the Bow Hero Saw
text: “Can you only shoot arrows while running away? Small potatoes. Might’ve been a decent attack in some console game, but it just shows your level, Itsuki. Look… right here. Though I doubt you could even hit it. Pathetic.”

Father pointed at his own chest, taunting Itsuki to try and land a hit. Still, “small potatoes”—now that was a phrase I’d thought about before too. It’s a derogatory term for those who do nothing but shoot from the back lines, I say. Rather harsh, if you ask me.

Personally, I’m quite fond of potatoes as a crop. Starting with regular potatoes, and sweet potatoes too. Father’s potato dishes are exquisite, I say. Daigaku imo, niku-jaga, even plain fluffed potatoes—making even those taste this good is a kind of talent, indeed. Come to think of it, the pigs in my memories always tried to make niku-jaga for some reason and always failed. Why is that, I wonder? They probably wanted to “win a man’s heart through his stomach,” as they say, but somehow always threw in some mysterious arrangement that ruined the dish. Meanwhile, Father’s niku-jaga was simple yet incredibly delicious. Even in the first world, Father used to make niku-jaga.

I heard him say it myself—that niku-jaga, curry, and stew were easy to throw together without much thought, so they were convenient. But I knew better. The secret fond stock Father used so generously in it turned the dish into something the villagers would practically fight over. There was never any left, but Father would deliberately set some aside to make niku-jaga croquettes too. Those were exquisite as well.
“I’m suddenly craving niku-jaga.”
“Why bring up… niku-jaga of all things, right now?”
Gator Guy and Rabbit Guy both turned to look at me.
“You said it! Then eat this! Bunker Shot!”

Just as I remembered, Itsuki—his anger flaring at Father’s taunt—closed in and unleashed a skill straight at Father’s chest. A heavy thud rang out as the impact passed through Father. Gator Guy and the others looked anxious, so I figured I’d better decide whether to paralyze them or just keep watch.
“One more step and I’ll paralyze you, I say.”
“Can’t move like this, then.”
“Ugh, I don’t even understand why we’re being watched by Spear Hero.”
Because if you do something unnecessary, it’ll trouble Father, of course. The just thing to do here was to trust Father and wait, indeed.
“What are we even supposed to do?”
“Cheer him on with high-pitched enthusiasm, I say. Like, ‘Kyaa! Father, you’re so wonderful! So sturdy!’ Something like that, I say.”
Gator Guy stared at me with half-lidded eyes, thoroughly exasperated. What, I say? Well, it’s the kind of dim-witted cheering pigs love to do.

“Now then, Rabbit Guy, you should turn into an adorable rabbit form and cheer Father on like a proper rabbit. If you cheer in the cute category, same as Panda, Father will smile and get motivated, I say.”
Whenever the Raph-species cheered him on, Father would smile, after all. Of course, Filo-tan and the others cheered too. So all Rabbit Guy needed to do was cheer in a rabbit-like way, I say.
“Concretely speaking, tilt your head to the side like this while making your eyes sparkle as much as possible, I say. Not quite on Filolial-sama’s level, but give it your all, indeed.”
“Why do I have to do something like that?”
“Because it’ll make Father happy, I say.”
“Is that actually true?”
“It’s true, indeed.”
Whenever I turned into an usaunny and approached going “Pet me, Father!”, he’d smile and pet me. So a rabbit form is guaranteed to have the effect of cheering Father up, without question.
“Hey… are you serious?”
“Well, if there’s nothing else we can do, at least I want to cheer him on, don’t I?”
Gator Guy cautioned Rabbit Guy. What, I say?
“Well, I suppose Gator Guy could never pull off this level of cuteness.”
“I think this man’s jealous.”
Gator Guy let out a deep sigh at that.
“…I’ll admit, maybe I’m a little bit envious of you.”
“No, no way!? That’s absolutely not a compliment I’m happy about! Let’s just focus on the match!”
Just as he said that, Itsuki, having failed to break through Father’s defense, fell speechless. Ah, I missed the line where Father said something like “not exactly unbreakable” or whatever it was.
“Next… it’s my turn.”
“What do you think a shield can even do!?”
Still holding the force of the impact he’d absorbed, Father pressed the shield right up against Itsuki. The shield’s counter effect triggered, sharp spikes emerging and sinking in.
“Guh… this is…”
Itsuki staggered, dizzy. Right then, Father pushed him down and pinned him.
“I see… so that’s the move you had.”
“Clever thinking, Iwatani-sama. I’ve been uneasy about this ever since we first met, but to think you had a method like this prepared… I’m impressed.”
Gator Guy and the others seemed to have figured out what had happened too.
“Well then, if you surrender now, I’ll let you go?”
“Wh-who would ever surrender!?”
“I see… then I’ll just keep you pinned down until you do.”
“H-hmph. No matter what Shield Naofumi does, my victory won’t waver!”
“We’ll see how long you can keep saying that.”
I recalled this exchange too. Father, what exactly were you planning to do next, I wonder? Surely it wasn’t just going to end there.
“Ugh… gh…”

The poison seemed to be taking effect, slowing Itsuki’s movements. And as he kept struggling, another one of the shield’s counters triggered, sealing off his magic entirely. Around this time, the Crimson Swine ought to be getting ready to make some unnecessary move, I say. If magic came flying, should I intercept it? Shooting down incoming spells myself seemed like a reasonable option. As I kept an eye on the Crimson Swine, Father glanced my way and gave me a wink. Then, just for an instant, his gaze flicked toward the Crimson Swine. It seemed he already knew something was coming, and that look toward me was a signal that I didn’t need to do anything. He gave the same kind of signal to Gator Guy and the others too. They apparently decided to stay quiet and watch, guessing something was about to happen. And then, just as Itsuki’s movements began to slow, the Crimson Swine, hidden amid the crowd, unleashed a wind spell.
“There we go.”
“Wha— Fguh!? Wh-what was that just now!?”

Father, still holding Itsuki down, grabbed his head and used it to intercept the wind magic the Crimson Swine had fired. A heavy impact struck Itsuki’s face, twisting it like he’d been punched, and he nearly went flying—but Father dispersed the force and pinned him back down onto the ground once more. Ohh… so this is what you can pull off if you know it’s coming. Truly, that’s Father for you, I say.
“Buu…”

Hm? Wasn’t that Lazy Pig? For a lazy pig, she’d cunningly erased her presence quite effectively, but I still spotted her. It looked like she was filming with some kind of image crystal. Itsuki wasn’t Takt, after all. Incidentally, Father apparently spotted her too—he said afterward it reminded him of a modern-day person filming video on a phone.
“Right now… ah, Hyu—”
“Damn it… ohh…”
Rabbit Guy and Gator Guy, realizing what had happened, clenched their fists tightly, then let out low whistles at Father’s masterful strategy.
“Now then, what did you see? Tell me, Itsuki.”
“Wh-what are y— No, let go of me!”

Itsuki’s fighting spirit seemed to falter for a moment, but he immediately resumed his struggle. Naturally, Father remained completely unharmed. Looking over at the Crimson Swine, her face practically screamed “Uh-oh!?” Serves you right! I say. I found myself both looking forward to and dreading how she’d try to explain her way out of this one. Of course, the referee was pretending not to notice—but since Itsuki himself had been shown the footage, there was no way to talk his way out of it now, I say.
“Y-you cowards, showing me some kind of illusion.”

Indeed, whether Itsuki was seeing double or simply in a state of confusion, he was straining to come up with some far-fetched excuse. Well, I suppose that’s what he wanted to believe, but his tone betrayed the doubt creeping in underneath.
